themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street conditions complaints surged to 192 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 34.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 458% spike (z-score 6.89)—suggesting acute pavement, pothole, or sidewalk deterioration affecting major thoroughfares in Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 192 street condition complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 34.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Street Condition ranks #3 in total 90-day volume (1,097 complaints), now concentrated in acute surge
reporting_angles: Map the worst-hit blocks this week; interview residents about specific hazards (potholes, cracked sidewalks, flooding)
Query DOT maintenance schedules and street resurfacing plans for the district—has a project stalled or been delayed?

themes_detail.label: Encampment Spike
themes_detail.summary: Homelessness-related encampment complaints jumped to 23 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 4.5 per week—a 411% spike (z-score 6.25)—indicating a sudden concentration of unsheltered individuals or new settlements in public spaces.
evidence: 23 encampment complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 4.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
No prior Reddit discussion or news mention suggests this is emerging story, not anticipated
reporting_angles: Locate the specific parks, transit hubs, or commercial blocks where encampments appeared; interview affected residents and business owners
Contact NYC Department of Homeless Services to understand whether a shelter closure, capacity issue, or policy change triggered the surge

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 5 complaints 3 weeks ago from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 3900% spike (z-score 14.74, highest severity)—suggesting organized bill-posting, graffiti, or signage campaigns now degrading public surfaces.
evidence: 5 illegal posting complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3900% spike, z-score: 14.74)
Highest z-score among all spikes, indicating most extreme statistical anomaly
Not currently sustained at this week's levels, but marks most dramatic single deviation from pattern
reporting_angles: Survey visible illegal postings across the district; photograph and map hotspots to identify any thematic campaign (political, commercial, gang-related)
Check with DSNY and local precinct whether enforcement actions occurred; determine if a removal backlog exists

themes_detail.label: Building Safety Concerns
themes_detail.summary: BEST/Site Safety complaints jumped to 3 last week from a 0.1 weekly baseline—a 2300% spike (z-score 8.69)—potentially flagging structural, demolition, or active construction hazards affecting public safety.
evidence: 3 BEST/Site Safety complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
643 total DOB permits filed in district over 90 days (112 new buildings, 431 alterations); active construction environment increases accident risk
Multiple active rezonings (21-31 46th Ave, 31-10/31-16 Hunters Point Ave) suggest ongoing development pressure and potential contractor oversight gaps
reporting_angles: Request DOB inspection logs and violation notices for recent construction sites; cross-reference with 311 complaints to identify problem contractors
Interview DOB and local precinct about whether any high-profile near-miss or injury incident triggered the spike

themes_detail.label: Rodent & Sanitation Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints rose to 12 three weeks ago from a 3.5 weekly baseline (243% spike, z-score 5.67), and unsanitary conditions on private property spiked to 3 last week from 0.2 baseline (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)—signaling coordinated pest and waste management breakdown.
evidence: 12 rodent complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 3.5 weekly baseline (243% increase, z-score: 5.67)
3 unsanitary condition (private property) complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1100% increase, z-score: 6.35)
Suggests systemic issue: either sanitation contractor failures, increased illegal dumping, or new food source attracting rodent populations
reporting_angles: Map rodent and unsanitary complaints by block; conduct street survey for visible waste, debris, or evidence of pest activity
Interview DSNY about commercial waste collection compliance and any sanitation enforcement actions in the district over the past month
